Definition: from G303 and G5455; to exclaim:--speak out.
BiblicalUsage: The word appears once: Elizabeth, filled with the Holy Ghost, spake out with a loud voice and said, 'Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb.' It is the speaking out — the cry of recognition when Mary comes through the door, and Elizabeth knows who the child is before Mary says a word.
TheologicalSignificance: One loud voice carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the greeting — Elizabeth speaking out what the Spirit showed her, that the mother of her Lord had come to her.
